faq.q: What is a titanium slit-valve protection shunt?
faq.a: A titanium slit-valve protection shunt is a precision-machined chamber shield component used in slit-valve plasma deposition protection shunt. Manufactured from Grade 2 CP-Ti (Bead Blasted) for optimal strength, corrosion resistance, and weight savings.

faq.q: What pressure rating for titanium slit-valve protection shunt?
faq.a: Pressure rating depends on grade, wall thickness, and temperature. Grade 2 CP-Ti pipe fittings are typically rated to Class 150 (285 psi) or Class 300 (740 psi) per ASME B16.5/B16.9. Higher ratings available with Grade 5.

faq.q: How is titanium slit-valve protection shunt manufactured?
faq.a: Titanium Slit-Valve Protection Shunt is manufactured using Precision CNC turning. Critical process controls include tool path optimization, coolant temperature management, and dimensional verification at each operation.

faq.q: What is the most common issue with titanium slit-valve protection shunt?
faq.a: The most common issue is surface contamination from iron pickup during machining requiring acid passivation (astm f86). Mitigation includes proper process control, material certification, and adherence to recommended installation procedures and torque values.

faq.q: What is the lead time for titanium slit-valve protection shunt?
faq.a: Standard lead time: 2-4 weeks depending on quantity and complexity. Rush orders available. Contact our team with your drawing and quantity for an accurate delivery quote.
